Putrefy

PYOO-truh-fy · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To putrefy to decay or rot and produce a foul smell.

Without refrigeration, the meat left on the counter started to putrefy within hours.

Worked Example

The biology teacher warned the class that the dissected specimen would putrefy quickly once removed from its preservative jar.

Putrefy is a fairly clinical, scientific word for the specific biological process of organic matter rotting and giving off a foul odor.

Antonyms

How Strong Is It? — spoil → putrefy → liquefy

spoil vs. putrefy

spoil vs. putrefy: Food can spoil without necessarily rotting all the way through.

liquefy vs. putrefy

liquefy vs. putrefy: Something so far gone it liquefies has decayed even further than simply putrefying.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — putr

Root — putr: rotten (from Latin putris, 'rotten')

Suffix — -efy

Suffix — -efy: to make, to cause to become (Latin -ficare; spelled -efy in a handful of English verbs like liquefy and stupefy)

Put it together

Put it together: putr ("rotten," from Latin putris) + -efy ("to make," the same ending as in liquefy) = to make rotten -- to decay.

Use the root in a new word: putrid

Use the root in a new word: putrid: The same root gives us "putrid," the everyday adjective for something that smells rotten.
